Pos.doc: An immutable position; block positions have integer coordinates.

params.name: dx
params.doc: Blocks to move along x.

params.name: dy
params.doc: Blocks to move along y.

params.name: dz
params.doc: Blocks to move along z.

offset.doc: Returns a new position moved by the given amounts.

toString.doc: Returns the position as text, for example `1, 64, -3`.

World.doc: One loaded dimension of the server.

time.doc: The dimension's game time in ticks.

dayTime.doc:
The time of day in ticks, 0 to 23999: 0 is sunrise, 6000 noon, 13000 nightfall and 18000 midnight. It follows this dimension's own clock, or the Overworld's in a dimension without one (such as the Nether).

Since runtime 1.5.1.

isRaining.doc:
Whether it is raining (or thundering) in this dimension. Always `false` in a dimension without an open sky, such as the Nether and the End. It changes as soon as the weather changes, while the rain on screen fades in over a few seconds.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

isThundering.doc:
Whether there is a thunderstorm in this dimension. Always `false` in a dimension without an open sky.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

getBlock.doc: Returns the block state at a position as `namespace:id[property=value,...]`.

params.name: state
params.doc: The block state, for example `minecraft:glowstone`.

setBlock.doc: Places a block state written as `namespace:id[property=value,...]`; returns `false` when the state does not parse or the block was not placed.

params.name: pos
params.doc: The block to break (the block that contains the position).

params.name: options
params.doc: `drops` (`true` by default): whether the block drops what it would drop when broken without a tool, as an explosion or `/setblock ... destroy` does.

breakBlock.doc:
Breaks a block as if it were mined, with the breaking sound and particles, leaving air (or the fluid it held); for example `world.breakBlock(e.pos, { drops: false })`. Returns `false` when there was nothing to break (air).

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: particle
params.doc: A particle type without options, for example `minecraft:flame` or a project particle such as `mymod:spark`, or a vanilla particle options object such as `{ type: "minecraft:dust", color: [1, 0.5, 0], scale: 1.5 }`.

params.name: options
params.type: { count?: number; spread?: number; speed?: number; motion?: [number, number, number]; force?: boolean }
params.doc: `count` particles (1 by default; at most 1000 with `motion`), placed at a random offset of about `spread` blocks on each axis (a Gaussian with that standard deviation, 0 by default) and moving at a random speed of about `speed` (0 by default). `motion` (`[x, y, z]` in blocks per tick) gives each particle exactly that velocity instead of the random one, sending one packet per particle; `speed` is then not used. `force` sends to players up to 512 blocks away and draws whatever their Particles setting, as `/particle ... force`.

spawnParticle.doc:
Spawns particles at a position for nearby players. A particle that does not decode (an unknown id, a type that needs options given as an id, an options object with a wrong field) is a `TypeError`.

Options objects, `motion` and `force`: since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The sound event id, for example `minecraft:block.note_block.bell`.

params.name: options
params.doc: The volume and pitch, 1 by default.

playSound.doc: Plays a sound event at a position for nearby players. The id can be a vanilla sound event or a project sound key (for example `mymod:block.chime`) once the project declares it in `sounds.json`.

params.name: command
params.doc: The command without a leading slash.

params.name: at
params.doc: Where the command runs: `~ ~ ~` is this position. Without it, the command runs at the world spawn point.

runCommand.doc: Runs a command as the server with permission level 2 and no output; returns the command's result count. Without `at` it runs at the world spawn point with no `@s`; pass `at` for position-relative commands, or use `Entity.runCommand` to run as an entity.

params.name: id
params.doc: The function id, for example `mymod:reward`.

params.name: at
params.doc: Where the function runs: `~ ~ ~` is this position. Without it, the function runs at the world spawn point.

runFunction.doc: Runs a data pack function as the server; returns `false` when the function does not exist. Without `at` it runs at the world spawn point with no `@s`; pass `at` for position-relative functions, or use `Entity.runFunction` to run as an entity.

params.name: id
params.doc: The entity type id, for example `minecraft:zombie`.

spawnEntity.doc: Spawns an entity of a type at a position; returns `undefined` when it could not be spawned.

params.name: pos
params.doc: Where the item appears, exactly (use `pos.offset(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)` for the middle of a block).

params.name: item
params.doc: The item; a count over the item's stack size is dropped as several stacks, at most 64 stacks (more is a `RangeError`).

dropItem.doc:
Drops an item on the ground as a block drops its loot, with a small random push; for example `world.dropItem(e.pos.offset(0.5, 1, 0.5), { id: "minecraft:diamond", count: 3 })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: radius
params.doc: The radius in blocks.

entitiesNear.doc: Returns the living entities within a radius of a position.

params.name: from
params.doc: Where the ray starts.

params.name: direction
params.doc: The direction as a vector, for example an entity's `look`; its length does not matter.

params.name: maxDistance
params.doc: How far the ray goes in blocks, at most 128 (more is a `RangeError`).

params.name: options
params.doc: What the ray stops at.

raycast.doc:
Casts a ray and returns the first block or entity it hits, or `undefined` when it hits nothing in range; for example `world.raycast(player.pos.offset(0, 1.6, 0), player.look, 20)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: pos
params.doc: The block position.

getContainer.doc:
Returns the container of the block at a position, or `undefined` when the block has no slots: chests, barrels, hoppers, furnaces, dispensers and the mod's own containers and machines have one, stone does not; for example `e.world.getContainer(e.pos)`. A double chest gives the half at the position.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: pos
params.doc: The centre of the explosion, exactly.

params.name: power
params.doc: The strength from 0 to 10 (anything else is a `RangeError`): 1 is about a fireball, 4 TNT, 6 a charged creeper.

params.name: options
params.doc: `fire` (`false` by default) sets fires around it; `breaksBlocks` (`true` by default) breaks blocks, which then drop as from a bed exploding (the `block_explosion_drop_decay` game rule applies). Entities are always hurt and pushed.

explode.doc:
Makes an explosion that no entity caused; for example `world.explode(e.pos, 2, { breaksBlocks: false })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: kind
params.doc: The new weather.

params.name: seconds
params.doc: How long it lasts, more than 0 and at most 1000000 (anything else is a `RangeError`); when left out, the game picks a length as `/weather` does.

setWeather.doc:
Sets the weather of the whole server (every dimension shares it), as `/weather` does; for example `world.setWeather("thunder", 60)`. Another kind is a `TypeError`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: radius
params.doc: The radius in blocks.

itemsNear.doc:
Returns the items lying on the ground (dropped, thrown or spilled) within a radius of a position; `entitiesNear` keeps returning living entities only. For example `for (const d of world.itemsNear(e.pos, 4)) if (d.item.id === "minecraft:rotten_flesh") d.remove();`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: id
params.doc: The game rule's id with its namespace, for example `mypack:mana_regen` (an `msm:game_rule` of the project) or `minecraft:keep_inventory`; a vanilla rule may leave out `minecraft:`.

gameRule.doc:
Returns a game rule's value: `true` or `false` for a rule that is on or off, a whole number for a number rule, or `undefined` when the id is no game rule of this game (a project rule that was not loaded, another mod's that is missing). Game rules belong to the whole server (every dimension shares them) and are saved with the world. An id that is not a valid id is a `TypeError`; for example `if (world.gameRule("mypack:mana_regen")) ...`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

params.name: id
params.doc: The game rule's id, as for `gameRule`.

params.name: value
params.doc: `true` or `false` for a rule that is on or off; a number for a number rule, rounded down and kept within the rule's lowest and highest values.

setGameRule.doc:
Sets a game rule for the whole server as `/gamerule` does: it is saved with the world and a mod's change listeners run. An unknown id, or a value of the other kind (a number for an on-or-off rule, `true` for a number rule, a number that is not finite), is a `TypeError`; for example `world.setGameRule("mypack:max_mana", 20)`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Entity.doc: A living entity, wrapped for scripts; check `isAlive` before using one held across ticks.

type.doc: The entity type id, for example `minecraft:zombie`.

world.doc: The world the entity is in.

health.doc: The current health in half hearts.

maxHealth.doc: The maximum health in half hearts.

isAlive.doc: Whether the entity is still alive and loaded.

isPlayer.doc: Whether the entity is a player.

name.doc: The entity's display name as plain text.

velocity.doc: The entity's motion in blocks per tick (x, y, z).

look.doc: The direction the entity looks, as a vector of length 1.

data.doc: Data saved on this entity for the script's namespace, at most 16 KiB per namespace; a player keeps it on respawn.

params.name: x
params.doc: Blocks per tick along x.

params.name: y
params.doc: Blocks per tick along y (up).

params.name: z
params.doc: Blocks per tick along z.

setVelocity.doc: Replaces the motion, so the game moves the entity smoothly, as a slime block or a wind charge does; each part is limited to 10. Players are pushed too.

params.name: x
params.doc: Blocks per tick along x.

params.name: y
params.doc: Blocks per tick along y (up).

params.name: z
params.doc: Blocks per tick along z.

addVelocity.doc: Adds to the motion, for example `entity.addVelocity(0, 1, 0)` for a jump; each part is limited to 10.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The damage in half hearts.

overloads.doc: Deals generic damage to the entity.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The damage in half hearts.

params.name: options
params.type: { type?: string; attacker?: Entity; direct?: Entity }
params.doc: The damage type id (for example `minecraft:magic`; `minecraft:generic` by default), the entity responsible and the entity that hit (a projectile, for example).

overloads.doc:
Deals damage of a type, from an attacker, to the entity, for example `target.damage(4, { type: "minecraft:player_attack", attacker: player })`; an unknown damage type is a script error.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

damage.doc: Deals generic damage to the entity.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The health to add in half hearts.

heal.doc: Heals the entity, up to its maximum health.

overloads.doc: Moves the entity to a position in its current world.

params.name: pos
params.doc: The position to move to.

params.name: options
params.type: { dimension?: string; yaw?: number; pitch?: number }
params.doc: The dimension id to move to (the current one by default) and the facing in degrees (unchanged by default).

overloads.doc:
Moves the entity to a position, in another dimension or facing another way, for example `player.teleport(pos, { dimension: "minecraft:the_nether" })`; the wrapper stays valid after the move.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

teleport.doc: Moves the entity to a position in its current world.

params.name: id
params.doc: The effect id, for example `minecraft:speed`.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: The duration in ticks.

params.name: amplifier
params.doc: The amplifier, 0 (level I) by default.

addEffect.doc: Gives the entity a mob effect.

params.name: id
params.doc: The effect id, for example `minecraft:speed` or one of your own.

hasEffect.doc: Returns whether the entity currently has the mob effect.

params.name: id
params.doc: The effect id, for example `minecraft:speed` or one of your own.

effectLevel.doc: Returns the level of the mob effect (the amplifier plus 1), or 0 when the entity does not have it.

params.name: id
params.doc: The effect id, for example `minecraft:speed` or one of your own.

removeEffect.doc: Removes the mob effect; returns `true` when the entity had it.

params.name: name
params.doc: The animation name, for example `animation.my_mob.attack`.

params.name: controller
params.doc: The animation controller, the entity's main one by default.

playAnimation.doc: Triggers a GeckoLib animation on an MSM entity; does nothing on other entities.

params.name: command
params.doc: The command without a leading slash.

runCommand.doc: Runs a command as and at this entity (`@s` is the entity, `~ ~ ~` is its position, in its facing) with permission level 2 and no output; returns the command's result count, or 0 when the entity is not in a server level.

params.name: id
params.doc: The function id, for example `mymod:reward`.

runFunction.doc: Runs a data pack function as and at this entity (`@s` is the entity); returns `false` when the function does not exist or the entity is not in a server level.

asPlayer.doc: Returns this entity as a player, or `undefined` when it is not one.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The equipment slot.

equipment.doc:
Returns a copy of the stack in an equipment slot, or `undefined` when it is empty; for example `entity.equipment("head")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The equipment slot.

params.name: item
params.doc: The new stack; `undefined` empties the slot.

setEquipment.doc:
Replaces the stack in an equipment slot, for example `zombie.setEquipment("mainhand", "minecraft:iron_sword")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: maxDistance
params.doc: How far the ray goes in blocks, at most 128 (more is a `RangeError`).

params.name: options
params.doc: What the ray stops at; it always passes through this entity.

raycast.doc:
Casts a ray from the entity's eyes along its look and returns the first block or entity it hits, or `undefined`; for example `player.raycast(5)?.block?.id`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

remove.doc:
Removes the entity from the world at once, without dropping loot or experience and without death events or a death animation (unlike `kill()`). A player cannot be removed: calling it on a player is a `TypeError`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

vehicle.doc:
What this entity rides, or `undefined` when it rides nothing: a project vehicle (then also a `Vehicle`, see `asVehicle()`), a boat, a minecart or a mount; for example `if (player.vehicle?.isVehicle) ...`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

passengers.doc:
The entities riding this one, in seat order (the first drives a vehicle); an empty array when none. A new array on every read.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

isVehicle.doc:
Whether this entity is a project vehicle (an `msm:vehicle`); `false` for players, mobs, boats and minecarts, even with riders.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

asVehicle.doc:
Returns this entity as a project vehicle with the `Vehicle` members, or `undefined` when it is not one; for example `const car = player.vehicle?.asVehicle()`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: vehicle
params.doc: What to get on: a mob, a boat, a minecart, a project vehicle or any other entity.

ride.doc:
Makes this entity get on another, as it would by itself: returns `true` when it now rides `vehicle`, `false` when it cannot (a full vehicle, a mob that takes no riders, sneaking, or for a short while after getting off something, vanilla's boarding cooldown). Riding itself, riding something that rides it, riding into another world and riding a player are refused (`false`), as with vanilla's `/ride`. An entity that rides something else gets off it first; for example `zombie.ride(chicken)`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

dismount.doc:
Makes this entity get off what it rides; returns `false` when it rides nothing. For example `if (player.vehicle) player.dismount()`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

isCreative.doc: Whether the player is in creative mode.

heldItem.doc: The item id in the player's main hand, or `undefined` when it is empty.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id, for example `minecraft:diamond`, or since runtime 1.5.1 an item with components, `{ id, count?, components? }`.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many; the item's own `count`, or 1, by default.

give.doc: Gives the player items; what does not fit in the inventory is dropped at their feet.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id.

hasItem.doc: Returns whether the player's inventory holds at least one of an item.

params.name: text
params.doc: The message as plain text.

sendMessage.doc: Sends a chat message to the player only.

inventory.doc:
The player's inventory, for example `player.inventory.count("minecraft:diamond")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

xpLevel.doc:
The player's experience level.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

xpPoints.doc:
The total experience points the player has collected.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

food.doc:
The food level, 0 to 20.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

saturation.doc:
The saturation level, 0 up to the food level.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

gameMode.doc:
The player's game mode, for example `"survival"`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: points
params.doc: The points to add; a negative number takes points away.

addXp.doc:
Gives the player experience points, for example `player.addXp(10)`; levels go up as the points fill them.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: levels
params.doc: The levels to add; a negative number takes levels away.

addXpLevels.doc:
Gives the player experience levels, for example `player.addXpLevels(1)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: levels
params.doc: The new level, 0 or more.

setXpLevels.doc:
Sets the player's experience level, for example `player.setXpLevels(30)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: level
params.doc: The food level, 0 to 20.

params.name: saturation
params.doc: The saturation, unchanged by default; it is never more than the food level.

setFood.doc:
Sets the player's food level and saturation, for example `player.setFood(20, 5)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: mode
params.doc: The game mode.

setGameMode.doc:
Changes the player's game mode, for example `player.setGameMode("adventure")`; returns `false` when the player was already in it.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: title
params.doc: The title as plain text.

params.name: options
params.type: { subtitle?: string; fadeIn?: number; stay?: number; fadeOut?: number }
params.doc: A subtitle and the fade in, stay and fade out times in ticks (10, 70 and 20 by default).

showTitle.doc:
Shows a title in the middle of the player's screen, for example `player.showTitle("Wave 3", { subtitle: "Get ready" })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: text
params.doc: The text as plain text.

showActionBar.doc:
Shows text above the player's hotbar for a few seconds, for example `player.showActionBar("Mana: 7")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

clearTitle.doc:
Removes the title and subtitle from the player's screen.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The HUD element's id (an `msm:hud` of the project), for example `mypack:mana`.

showHud.doc:
Shows a HUD element to this player, also one that starts hidden, until `hideHud`; an element with a `show` rule (such as only in a vehicle) still follows it. Returns `false` when the id is no HUD element of this game (logged once), else `true`; for example `player.showHud("mypack:mana")`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: id
params.doc: The HUD element's id (an `msm:hud` of the project), for example `mypack:mana`.

hideHud.doc:
Hides a HUD element from this player until `showHud`. Returns `false` when the id is no HUD element of this game (logged once), else `true`; for example `player.hideHud("mypack:mana")`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: id
params.doc: The HUD element's id (an `msm:hud` of the project), for example `mypack:mana`.

params.name: value
params.doc: A number (for a bar, icons or a number) or a text (cut to 256 characters).

setHud.doc:
Sets the value a HUD element shows this player, as the `set_hud` action does; the player's screen updates within a quarter of a second. For an element that reads its value from the game (a score, the player or the vehicle) the next value that differs replaces it. Returns `false` when the id is no HUD element of this game (logged once) or the number is not finite, else `true`; for example `player.setHud("mypack:mana", 7)`. Any other value is a `TypeError`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: id
params.doc: A custom statistic's id, for example `mypack:jumps_over_lava` (an `msm:stat` of the project) or vanilla's `minecraft:jump`.

stat.doc:
Returns this player's value of a custom statistic, 0 when it was never counted (a distance in centimetres, a time in ticks). An unknown id is a `TypeError`; for example `player.stat("mypack:coins_found")`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

params.name: id
params.doc: A custom statistic's id, as for `stat`.

params.name: amount
params.doc: How much to add, rounded down; a negative amount takes away, never below 0.

addStat.doc:
Adds to this player's value of a custom statistic and returns the new value. It is saved with the player, shown in the statistics screen and moves the scores of scoreboard objectives that count it (criterion `minecraft.custom:<namespace>.<path>`). An unknown id or an amount that is not a finite number is a `TypeError`; for example `player.addStat("mypack:coins_found", 1)`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

params.name: id
params.doc: The dialog's id, for example `mypack:welcome` (a dialog in the project's data pack) or one of vanilla's.

openDialog.doc:
Opens a dialog on this player's screen, as `/dialog show` does. Returns `false` when the id is no dialog of this game (logged once), else `true`; for example `player.openDialog("mypack:welcome")`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

BlockRef.doc: A block in the world at the time of the event.

ItemRef.doc: An item stack, copied at the time it was read: changing the game later does not change it.

count.doc: The number of items in the stack.

name.doc:
The item's display name as plain text, its custom name when it has one, for example `Diamond Sword`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

maxCount.doc:
The most items one stack of this item can hold, for example 64 or 1.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

damage.doc:
The damage the item has taken, 0 when it is new or cannot be damaged.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

maxDamage.doc:
The damage the item can take before it breaks, 0 when it cannot be damaged.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The data component id, for example `minecraft:enchantments`.

hasComponent.doc:
Returns whether the item has a data component, for example `item.hasComponent("minecraft:custom_name")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The data component id, for example `minecraft:damage`.

getComponent.doc:
Returns a copy of a data component's value as JSON (the form `/give` and data packs use), or `undefined` when the item does not have it; for example `item.getComponent("minecraft:damage")` is a number. At most 64 KiB of JSON is returned.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

contents.doc:
The items this item holds, as copies: a bag's or other container item's contents (shulker boxes too) in slot order, then a bundle's in the bundle's order; empty slots are left out, and an item that holds nothing gives an empty array. Read-only: change a bag by giving the player a new stack.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

DataStore.doc: Saved data of one script namespace, on an entity or with the world: values are JSON values, copied in and out, and survive `/reload`, restarts, death and dimension changes.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key, at most 64 characters.

get.doc: Returns a copy of the value stored under a key, or `undefined` when there is none.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key, at most 64 characters.

params.name: value
params.doc: A JSON value: a string, a finite number, a boolean, `null`, an array or a plain object of these.

set.doc: Stores a copy of a JSON value under a key; any other value is a `TypeError`, and a key longer than 64 characters or a store over its size limit is a script error that leaves the old value.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key, at most 64 characters.

remove.doc: Removes the value stored under a key; returns `true` when there was one.

params.name: key
params.doc: The key, at most 64 characters.

has.doc: Returns `true` when a value is stored under a key.

keys.doc: Returns the keys stored for this script's namespace.

world.doc: The world (dimension) the event happened in.

player.doc: The player who used it.

cancel.doc: Cancels the event: the block and the held item are not used.

BlockBreakEvent.doc: A player is about to break a block.

player.doc: The player breaking it.

cancel.doc: Cancels the event: the block stays in place.

ItemUseEvent.doc: A player used (right-clicked) the held item in the air.

player.doc: The player using it.

cancel.doc: Cancels the event: the item is not used.

player.doc: The player who used it.

cancel.doc: Cancels the event: the interaction does not happen.

EntityHurtEvent.doc: A living entity is about to take damage.

attacker.doc: The entity that caused the damage, when there is one.

cancel.doc: Cancels the event: the entity takes no damage.

source.doc:
The damage type id, for example `minecraft:fall` or `minecraft:player_attack`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

direct.doc:
The entity that hit, when there is one: an arrow rather than its shooter, for example.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

attacker.doc: The entity that killed it, when there is one.

killer.doc:
Who the game credits with the kill, as its kill scores and death message do: the attacker of a direct hit, and also the last entity that hurt it a short while before a death with no attacker (a knock into the void, a fall, lava); `undefined` when nobody is credited. For example `msm.events.on("entity.death", (e) => { const k = e.killer?.asPlayer(); if (e.entity.isPlayer && k) k.sendMessage("You got " + e.entity.name); });`.

Since runtime 1.5.10.

player.doc: The player who joined.

ServerStartedEvent.doc: The server finished starting; `world` is the overworld.

ServerTickEvent.doc: The server finished a tick; `world` is the overworld.

tick.doc: The number of ticks since the server started.

ActionEvent.doc: A definition event ran a `run_script` action that names this handler.

owner.doc: The id of the block, item or entity definition whose event ran.

event.doc: The definition event id, for example `msm:on_interact`.

pos.doc: The position the event happened at.

block.doc: The block involved, when there is one.

entity.doc: The entity involved, when there is one: the entity that stepped on a block (a mob, an item or a minecart as well as a player), for example.

player.doc: The player involved, when there is one.

other.doc: The other entity involved, when there is one: the entity that stepped on a block, the entity a thrown item hit, or the holder of a status effect.

args.doc:
When the action runs in a project command's own event (its `event`, and the events it triggers): the values typed, by argument name, as the `command` event's `args` gives them (the types of Script API 1.7 as their ids or text, see the guide). `undefined` for every other action. A new object for each event.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Inventory.doc:
A player's inventory; slots are read and written straight away, for example `player.inventory.set(0, "minecraft:torch")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

size.doc:
The number of numbered slots, 36: 0 to 8 are the hotbar and 9 to 35 the main inventory.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

selectedSlot.doc:
The selected hotbar slot, 0 to 8.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot, 0 to 35 or an equipment slot name.

get.doc:
Returns a copy of the stack in a slot, or `undefined` when the slot is empty; for example `player.inventory.get("offhand")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot, 0 to 35 or an equipment slot name.

params.name: item
params.doc: The new stack; `undefined` empties the slot.

set.doc:
Replaces the stack in a slot, for example `player.inventory.set("head", "minecraft:carved_pumpkin")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id, for example `minecraft:diamond`.

count.doc:
Returns how many of an item the inventory holds over all slots, for example `player.inventory.count("minecraft:diamond")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id.

params.name: count
params.doc: How many to remove; all of them when omitted.

remove.doc:
Removes up to a number of an item from the inventory and returns how many were removed, for example `player.inventory.remove("minecraft:emerald", 5)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id.

find.doc:
Returns the first numbered slot that holds an item, or -1 when none does; for example `player.inventory.find("minecraft:compass")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot, 0 to 35 or an equipment slot name.

params.name: id
params.doc: The data component id, for example `minecraft:custom_name`.

params.name: value
params.doc: The component's JSON value; `undefined` removes the component.

setComponent.doc:
Sets or removes a data component of the stack in a slot, for example `player.inventory.setComponent(0, "minecraft:custom_name", "Lucky")`; does nothing on an empty slot, and a value that does not decode or validate is a script error (at most 64 KiB of JSON).

Since runtime 1.5.1.

BossBar.doc:
A boss bar shown at the top of the screen of the players added to it; it belongs to the script's namespace, is not saved, and is removed on `/reload` and when the server stops, for example `msm.bossBars.create("countdown", { title: "Time left" })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: title
params.doc: The title as plain text.

setTitle.doc:
Changes the bar's title.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: progress
params.doc: How full the bar is, 0 to 1; values outside are clamped.

setProgress.doc:
Changes how full the bar is, for example `bar.setProgress(0.5)`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: color
params.doc: The colour.

setColor.doc:
Changes the bar's colour, for example `bar.setColor("red")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: style
params.doc: The style.

setStyle.doc:
Changes the bar's style, for example `bar.setStyle("notched_10")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: player
params.doc: The player.

addPlayer.doc:
Shows the bar to a player; adding a player twice does nothing.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: player
params.doc: The player.

removePlayer.doc:
Hides the bar from a player.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

players.doc:
Returns the players the bar is shown to.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

remove.doc:
Hides the bar from everyone and removes it, so `msm.bossBars.get` no longer finds it.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

RayHit.doc:
What a ray hit, from `World.raycast` or `Entity.raycast`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

kind.doc:
Whether the ray hit a block or an entity.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

pos.doc:
The exact point the ray hit.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

distance.doc:
The distance from the ray's start to the hit in blocks.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

block.doc:
The block hit, when `kind` is `"block"`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

face.doc:
The face of the block the ray hit, when `kind` is `"block"`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

entity.doc:
The entity hit, when `kind` is `"entity"`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

PlayerTickEvent.doc:
A player's turn of the `player.tick` interval came round.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.doc:
The player.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

PlayerRespawnEvent.doc:
A player respawned after dying or returned from the End; `world` is the world they respawned in.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.doc:
The player, already in the new world.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

PlayerLeaveEvent.doc:
A player is leaving the server.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.doc:
The player leaving.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

PlayerChangeDimensionEvent.doc:
A player moved to another dimension; `world` is the new one.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.doc:
The player who moved.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

from.doc:
The dimension id the player left, for example `minecraft:overworld`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

to.doc:
The dimension id the player arrived in, for example `minecraft:the_nether`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

PlayerChatEvent.doc:
A player sent a chat message.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.doc:
The player who sent it.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

message.doc:
The message as plain text.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

cancel.doc:
Cancels the event: nobody sees the message.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

EntityDamagedEvent.doc:
A living entity took damage.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

entity.doc:
The entity that was damaged.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

amount.doc:
The damage it took in half hearts, after armour and effects.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

attacker.doc:
The entity that caused the damage, when there is one.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

direct.doc:
The entity that hit, when there is one: an arrow rather than its shooter, for example.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

source.doc:
The damage type id, for example `minecraft:fall`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Container.doc:
The slots of a block with a container, from `World.getContainer`; read and written straight away, and writes update comparators next to the block, for example `world.getContainer(pos)?.add("minecraft:coal")`. Using it after the block is removed or replaced is a script error.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

size.doc:
The number of slots, numbered 0 to `size - 1`; for example 27 for a chest.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot, 0 to `size - 1`.

get.doc:
Returns a copy of the stack in a slot, or `undefined` when the slot is empty; for example `container.get(0)`. A slot outside 0 to `size - 1` is a `RangeError`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot, 0 to `size - 1`.

params.name: item
params.doc: The new stack, at most the slot's stack size; `undefined` empties the slot.

set.doc:
Replaces the stack in a slot and returns `true`, or returns `false` and changes nothing when the container does not take that item in that slot (a furnace's result slot, a container item in a crate that keeps its contents); for example `container.set(0, { id: "minecraft:torch", count: 16 })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: item
params.doc: The item id, for example `minecraft:coal`.

count.doc:
Returns how many of an item the container holds over all slots, for example `container.count("minecraft:coal")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: item
params.doc: The stack to put in; its count may be more than one stack.

add.doc:
Puts a stack in as a hopper would, filling matching stacks and then empty slots in slot order and skipping slots that do not take the item, whatever side hoppers may use; returns what did not fit, or `undefined` when everything fit. For example `const left = container.add({ id: "minecraft:coal", count: 64 })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Vehicle.doc:
A project vehicle (an `msm:vehicle`): an `Entity` with fuel, damage, ammunition and a driver, read and written straight away on the server. Every vehicle object a script gets (`asVehicle()`, `vehicle.*` events, `entitiesNear`) has these members; for example `msm.events.on("vehicle.mounted", (e) => e.vehicle.setFuel(1200))`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

fuel.doc:
Ticks of driving left in the tank; always 0 for a vehicle that needs no fuel.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: Ticks of driving.

setFuel.doc:
Sets the fuel, rounded down and kept between 0 and the tank's capacity (0 for a vehicle that needs no fuel); for example `vehicle.setFuel(vehicle.fuel + 200)`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

damageTaken.doc:
The damage the vehicle has taken, from 0 (as new) up to its `health.max`; it never heals by itself. (`damage(amount)`, inherited from `Entity`, deals more.)

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The damage; below 0 counts as 0.

setDamageTaken.doc:
Sets the damage taken; 0 repairs it fully. At or above the vehicle's `health.max` it is destroyed as by damage: its `on_destroy` and `vehicle.destroyed` (without a player) run, the riders get out, it explodes when it is set to and drops its item and storage.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: weapon
params.doc: The weapon's `id` in the vehicle's definition, or its index from 0.

ammo.doc:
Returns the rounds loaded in a weapon; 0 for a weapon without ammunition. An unknown id or index is a `RangeError`; for example `vehicle.ammo("cannon")`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: weapon
params.doc: The weapon's `id` in the vehicle's definition, or its index from 0.

params.name: rounds
params.doc: The rounds, rounded down.

setAmmo.doc:
Sets the rounds loaded in a weapon, kept between 0 and its capacity (0 for a weapon without ammunition). An unknown id or index is a `RangeError`; for example `vehicle.setAmmo(0, 10)`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

driver.doc:
The player in the first seat, who drives, or `undefined`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

KeyPressedEvent.doc:
A player pressed a project key bind.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who pressed the key.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

key.doc:
The key bind's id, for example `mypack:dash`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

KeyReleasedEvent.doc:
A player let go of a project key bind.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who let go of the key.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

key.doc:
The key bind's id, for example `mypack:dash`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

VehicleMountedEvent.doc:
A player got into a project vehicle.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who got in; `e.vehicle.driver` tells whether they drive.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

VehicleDismountedEvent.doc:
A player got out of a project vehicle.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who got out.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

VehicleFiredEvent.doc:
A project vehicle's weapon fired one shot.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who fired.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

weapon.doc:
The weapon's `id` in the vehicle's definition.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

VehicleDestroyedEvent.doc:
A project vehicle is being destroyed.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

vehicle.doc:
The vehicle, still in the world with its riders.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player who destroyed it, or `undefined` (a mob, an explosion, `setDamage`).

Since runtime 1.5.2.

DroppedItem.doc:
An item lying in the world, as `World.itemsNear` finds it. Once it is gone (picked up, merged into another stack, despawned or removed) `remove()` and `setItem()` do nothing.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

item.doc:
A copy of the stack it holds now.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

pos.doc:
Where it is now, exactly.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

age.doc:
How long it has been lying there in ticks (20 a second); vanilla removes an item at 6000 (five minutes).

Since runtime 1.5.2.

owner.doc:
The UUID of the entity that dropped or threw it, or `undefined` when nothing did or that entity is not in the world (a player who has left).

Since runtime 1.5.2.

remove.doc:
Removes the item from the world at once; it drops nothing else.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

params.name: item
params.doc: The new stack; a count over the item's stack size holds the stack size.

setItem.doc:
Replaces the stack it holds; for example `d.setItem({ id: "minecraft:diamond", count: 3 })`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

BlockPlaceEvent.doc:
A player is about to place a block from a block item.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

pos.doc:
Where the block would go (the clicked block itself when it can be replaced, such as grass, else the block next to the clicked face).

Since runtime 1.5.2.

block.doc:
The id of the block the item places, for example `minecraft:oak_planks`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

item.doc:
The item being placed, as held before the placement.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

player.doc:
The player placing it.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

cancel.doc:
Cancels the event: the block is not placed, the item is not used up and the player's screen is corrected.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

ExplosionEvent.doc:
Something is about to explode.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

pos.doc:
The centre of the explosion, exactly.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

radius.doc:
The explosion's power: 4 for TNT, 3 for a creeper, 6 for a charged creeper, 5 for a bed or respawn anchor.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

source.doc:
The entity that exploded (the primed TNT, the creeper, the fireball, the wind charge), or `undefined` for a block such as a bed or respawn anchor, or `World.explode`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

cause.doc:
The type id of `source`, for example `minecraft:tnt` or `minecraft:creeper`, or `"block"` when there is no source.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

cancel.doc:
Cancels the event: nothing breaks and nothing is hurt or pushed. The bang and the smoke may still be seen and heard.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

keepBlocks.doc:
Keeps every block safe: entities are still hurt and pushed, but no block breaks, drops or catches fire. `cancel()` wins when both are called.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

CommandEvent.doc:
A project command ran.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

id.doc:
The command's id in the project, for example `mypack:greet`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

name.doc:
The command's name, as typed without the slash, for example `greet`; also when one of its other names was typed.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

source.doc:
Who ran it: the player (see `asPlayer()`) or the entity of an `execute as`, or `undefined` for the server console or a command block.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

args.doc:
The values typed, by argument name: numbers as numbers, words and text as strings, `true` or `false`, a player or entity as its UUID, players as an array of names, a position or block position as `[x, y, z]`, an item or block as its id; an optional argument that was not typed is missing. A new object for each event.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

ItemCraftedEvent.doc:
A player crafted something.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who crafted it.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

item.doc:
What was made, with `count` the number made by this one craft.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

count.doc:
How many were made by this one craft (a shift-click that crafts three times is three events).

Since runtime 1.5.3.

ItemPickedUpEvent.doc:
A player picked up an item from the ground.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who picked it up.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

item.doc:
The item, with `count` the number taken.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

count.doc:
How many went into the inventory; less than were on the ground when the inventory was nearly full.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

PlayerAteEvent.doc:
A player finished eating or drinking something.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who ate or drank.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

item.doc:
One of what was eaten or drunk, as it was before.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

PlayerSleptEvent.doc:
A player lay down in a bed.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who lay down.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

pos.doc:
Where the bed is (the block the player sleeps on).

Since runtime 1.5.3.

PlayerWokeEvent.doc:
A player got out of a bed.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who got up.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

pos.doc:
Where the bed is.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

PlayerAdvancementEvent.doc:
A player completed an advancement.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.doc:
The player who completed it.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

advancement.doc:
The advancement's id, for example `minecraft:story/mine_stone` or `mypack:first_coin`.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

msm.doc: The MSM runtime API, available to every script.

version.doc: The version of the running `msm_runtime` mod.

info.doc: Logs a message at information level.

warn.doc: Logs a message at warning level.

error.doc: Logs a message at error level.

log.doc: Writes to the server log as `[msm_runtime] <script id>: <message>`.

overloads.doc: Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) a block. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs before a player breaks a block. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) a held item. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) an entity. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs before a living entity takes damage. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs after a living entity dies. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs when a player joins the server. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs once the server has started. Several handlers run in registration order.
Runs at the end of every server tick (20 times a second); keep the handler cheap. Several handlers run in registration order.

params.name: options
params.doc: How often the handler runs for each player in ticks: 20 by default; a value under 5 counts as 5.

overloads.doc:
Runs for each online player every `interval` ticks (20 by default; a value under 5 runs every 5 ticks), spread over the interval by player; for example `msm.events.on("player.tick", (e) => { ... }, { interval: 40 })`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs after a player respawns, for example to give a starting kit back. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs when a player leaves the server. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs after a player moves to another dimension, for example through a Nether portal. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs before a player's chat message is sent to the other players. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs after a living entity took damage, with the final amount; also for the killing blow, before entity.death. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

Runs when a player presses a project key bind (an `msm:key_bind`) and the press counts (its `when` and cooldown allow it), after the key bind's own `msm:on_press`; the runtime's own vehicle keys are not reported. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs when a player lets go of a project key bind whose press counted, after the key bind's own `msm:on_release`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs when a player gets into a project vehicle, after its `on_mount`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs when a player gets out of a project vehicle (also when it is destroyed or they leave the game), after its `on_dismount`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs after each shot of a project vehicle's weapon, after the weapon's `on_fire`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs when a project vehicle is destroyed, after its `on_destroy` and before its riders get out (`vehicle.dismounted` follows for each). Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs before a player places a block from a block item, wherever the block would go. Placing by dispensers, endermen and commands does not fire it. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs before anything explodes: TNT, creepers, fireballs, wind charges, beds, respawn anchors and `World.explode`. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs when a player or the server runs one of the project's commands, after the command's function and event and before its message back. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

Runs each time a player crafts something: in the inventory's grid, at a crafting table (once per craft of a shift-click) or by taking the result of a furnace and the other result slots of the game's menus. Crafters and other machines do not fire it. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Runs when a player picks up an item from the ground, also when only part of it fits. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Runs when a player finishes eating or drinking something (food, a potion, milk, a project bottle); a meal that was stopped before the end does not fire it. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Runs when a player lies down in a bed. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Runs when a player gets out of a bed: in the morning, by leaving the bed, or woken. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

Runs when a player completes an advancement, by playing or by `/advancement`; the recipe advancements that unlock recipe book entries (`<namespace>:recipes/...`) do not fire it. Several handlers run in registration order.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

on.doc: Registers a handler for a game event.

params.name: id
params.doc: The handler id, a resource location such as `mymod:ore_glow`.

define.doc: Defines a named handler for `run_script` actions; a later definition with the same id replaces it.

actions.doc: Named handlers that definition events call through the `run_script` action.

params.name: ticks
params.doc: The delay in ticks, 1 or more.

schedule.doc: Runs a function after a number of server ticks; pending calls are cleared when scripts reload.

storage.doc: Data saved with the world for the script's namespace, at most 1 MiB per namespace; unlike `msm.schedule`, it survives `/reload` and restarts.

bossBars.doc:
Boss bars of the script's namespace, at most 32; they are not saved and are removed on `/reload` and when the server stops.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The bar's name within the script's namespace, for example `countdown`.

params.name: options
params.type: { title: string; color?: BossBarColor; style?: BossBarStyle; progress?: number }
params.doc: The title, the colour (`"white"` by default), the style (`"progress"` by default) and how full it is (1 by default).

create.doc:
Creates a boss bar shown to nobody yet, replacing a bar of the same name; for example `msm.bossBars.create("countdown", { title: "Time left", color: "red" })`. A 33rd bar is a script error.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: id
params.doc: The bar's name.

get.doc:
Returns the boss bar of a name, or `undefined` when there is none.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

params.name: dimension
params.doc: The dimension id, for example `minecraft:the_nether`.

getWorld.doc:
Returns a loaded dimension, or `undefined` when the server has none of that id; for example `msm.getWorld("minecraft:the_end")`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

players.doc:
Returns the players online, for example `msm.players().length`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

block.interact.doc: Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) a block.

block.break.doc: Runs before a player breaks a block.

item.use.doc: Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) a held item.

entity.interact.doc: Runs when a player uses (right-clicks) an entity.

entity.hurt.doc: Runs before a living entity takes damage.

entity.death.doc: Runs after a living entity dies.

player.join.doc: Runs when a player joins the server.

server.started.doc: Runs once the server has started.

server.tick.doc: Runs at the end of every server tick (20 times a second); keep the handler cheap.

player.tick.doc:
Runs for each online player every `interval` ticks (20 by default; a value under 5 runs every 5 ticks), spread over the interval by player; for example `msm.events.on("player.tick", (e) => { ... }, { interval: 40 })`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.respawn.doc:
Runs after a player respawns, for example to give a starting kit back.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.leave.doc:
Runs when a player leaves the server.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.changeDimension.doc:
Runs after a player moves to another dimension, for example through a Nether portal.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

player.chat.doc:
Runs before a player's chat message is sent to the other players.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

entity.damaged.doc:
Runs after a living entity took damage, with the final amount; also for the killing blow, before entity.death.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

key.pressed.doc:
Runs when a player presses a project key bind (an `msm:key_bind`) and the press counts (its `when` and cooldown allow it), after the key bind's own `msm:on_press`; the runtime's own vehicle keys are not reported.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

key.released.doc:
Runs when a player lets go of a project key bind whose press counted, after the key bind's own `msm:on_release`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

vehicle.mounted.doc:
Runs when a player gets into a project vehicle, after its `on_mount`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

vehicle.dismounted.doc:
Runs when a player gets out of a project vehicle (also when it is destroyed or they leave the game), after its `on_dismount`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

vehicle.fired.doc:
Runs after each shot of a project vehicle's weapon, after the weapon's `on_fire`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

vehicle.destroyed.doc:
Runs when a project vehicle is destroyed, after its `on_destroy` and before its riders get out (`vehicle.dismounted` follows for each).

Since runtime 1.5.2.

block.place.doc:
Runs before a player places a block from a block item, wherever the block would go. Placing by dispensers, endermen and commands does not fire it.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

world.explosion.doc:
Runs before anything explodes: TNT, creepers, fireballs, wind charges, beds, respawn anchors and `World.explode`.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

command.doc:
Runs when a player or the server runs one of the project's commands, after the command's function and event and before its message back.

Since runtime 1.5.2.

item.crafted.doc:
Runs each time a player crafts something: in the inventory's grid, at a crafting table (once per craft of a shift-click) or by taking the result of a furnace and the other result slots of the game's menus. Crafters and other machines do not fire it.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

item.picked_up.doc:
Runs when a player picks up an item from the ground, also when only part of it fits.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.ate.doc:
Runs when a player finishes eating or drinking something (food, a potion, milk, a project bottle); a meal that was stopped before the end does not fire it.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.slept.doc:
Runs when a player lies down in a bed.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.woke.doc:
Runs when a player gets out of a bed: in the morning, by leaving the bed, or woken.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

player.advancement.doc:
Runs when a player completes an advancement, by playing or by `/advancement`; the recipe advancements that unlock recipe book entries (`<namespace>:recipes/...`) do not fire it.

Since runtime 1.5.3.

params.name: id
params.doc: A relative id such as "./util" or "../lib/shapes" (a script of the same mod and namespace), or "msm:runtime".

require.doc: Loads another script of the same mod and namespace by a relative id and returns its module.exports (each script runs once; cycles see partial exports); require("msm:runtime") returns the msm module.

ItemSpec.type: string | { id: string; count?: number; components?: Record<string, unknown> }
ItemSpec.doc:
An item to give or put in a slot: an item id such as `"minecraft:diamond"`, or `{ id, count?, components? }` where `components` maps component ids to their JSON values, for example `{ id: "minecraft:diamond_sword", components: { "minecraft:custom_name": "Edge" } }`; components that do not decode or validate are a script error, and at most 64 KiB of component JSON is accepted per call.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

EquipmentSlot.doc:
An equipment slot of a living entity.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

InventorySlot.doc:
A player inventory slot: 0 to 8 are the hotbar, 9 to 35 the main inventory, or an equipment slot name; any other value is a `RangeError`.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

BossBarColor.doc:
The colour of a boss bar.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

BossBarStyle.doc:
The style of a boss bar: one continuous bar or one divided into 6, 10, 12 or 20 notches.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

RaycastOptions.type: { fluids?: boolean; entities?: boolean; ignore?: Entity }
RaycastOptions.doc:
What a ray stops at: `fluids` (false by default) makes fluid surfaces count as blocks, `entities` (true by default) lets the ray hit living entities, and `ignore` is an entity the ray passes through.

Since runtime 1.5.1.

ParticleOptions.doc:
A vanilla particle options object: `type` names a particle type and the other fields are that type's options, as in vanilla's particle JSON, for example `{ type: "minecraft:dust", color: [1, 0.5, 0], scale: 1.5 }`, `{ type: "minecraft:block", block_state: "minecraft:stone" }` or `{ type: "minecraft:item", item: { id: "minecraft:diamond" } }`; fields that do not decode are a script error.

Since runtime 1.5.1.
